clue.text: Circle small lake surrounding hotel

indicators.note: to surround something is to sit around it, so the first pair of pieces wraps round the last

blocks.note: wee is Scottish and informal for small
L is the map abbreviation for lake
H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A little lake with a hotel on its shore, ringed round as if seen from above.
explanation.walkthrough: The hotel's H goes in after the first letter of WEE, splitting it as W-H-EEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheel is a round disc or ring, so the noun circle is a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Cricketer's wife to pass time off with Guardian

indicators.note: something taken off is removed, so one letter drops out of the word for a pass

blocks.note: W is the standard abbreviation for wife
a ticket is a pass that admits you
T is the abbreviation for time
a keeper guards something

explanation.surface: A cricket player's wife whiles away the hours with a copy of the Guardian newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: TICKET loses its T to leave ICKET. 'Guardian' looks like the newspaper this puzzle appears in, but it is just a keeper.
explanation.definitionFit: The wicketkeeper is the fielding player who stands behind the stumps, so he is one particular cricketer.

clue.text: Inform on measures taken around daybreak

indicators.note: things taken around something enclose it, one on each side

blocks.note: an en is a printer's measure of width, and the plural gives two of them
daybreak is first light

explanation.surface: Someone tells tales on others' precautions taken at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inform on' reads as one phrase meaning grass, but only 'Inform' is the definition. The two ens sit either side of LIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlighten someone is to give them knowledge, which is what informing them does.

clue.text: Cricketer's swallowed very small bug

indicators.note: what is swallowed ends up inside, so one piece goes into the middle of the other

blocks.note: Brian Lara, the West Indian batsman
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: A cricketer has accidentally gulped down a tiny insect.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'has'. Brian Lara is a famous West Indian batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A larva is the young grub stage of an insect, a small creature loosely called a bug.

clue.text: Literary midget who's a library member?

blocks.note: first meaning: one of the tiny people in Mary Norton's children's books The ...
second meaning: someone who takes books out of a library

explanation.surface: A tiny character from a novel turns out to hold a library card.
explanation.walkthrough: The Borrowers are little people living under the floorboards in Mary Norton's books.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both one of Norton's little people and anyone who borrows books from a lending library.

clue.text: Northern town's holding day to obtain top advice on finance

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter
something holding other things keeps them inside it

blocks.note: Bury is a town in Greater Manchester
D is the abbreviation for day
to get is to obtain
first letter of advice

explanation.surface: A northern town hosts a day where people come for the best financial advice.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is a town near Manchester in the north of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Budgetary means relating to a budget, so it describes anything concerning finance.

clue.text: Costume for royal order?

blocks.note: R is short for royal, as in RN
the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A question about what a monarch wears for a ceremonial order.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE is an honour in the Order of the British Empire, awarded by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A robe is a long formal garment, which counts as a costume or outfit.

clue.text: Make huge fuss about old veteran being without free carer

indicators.note: letters set free are released from their order and can be rearranged
being without something here means being on the outside of it, wrapping it

blocks.note: O is short for old
vet is the American short form of veteran
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old soldier makes a scene when left without a free person to look after him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as 'lacking', but here it has its old sense of 'outside'.
explanation.definitionFit: To overreact is to respond more strongly than needed, which is making a huge fuss.

clue.text: In Paris she takes name of Miss MacArthur

blocks.note: elle is French for she
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A woman in Paris borrows the name of a famous British woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Ellen MacArthur is the British yachtswoman who sailed solo round the world in record time.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Ellen MacArthur, the record-breaking solo sailor, is the example; Miss gives her as an unmarried woman.

clue.text: State sugar crop's initially levelled to earth by pest

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: a US state
sugar beet is grown for sugar
first letter of levelled
E is the abbreviation for earth in electrical wiring

explanation.surface: A state's sugar harvest has been flattened to the ground by some pest.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Colorado beetle is a striped insect that destroys potato crops, a notorious farm pest.

clue.text: Broken agreements don't half cause disaffection

indicators.note: something broken is smashed up, so these letters are reassembled in a new order
only half of the word before it is kept, here its closing half

blocks.note: taken as written
the back half of don't, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Broken promises do cause bad feeling, if not entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't half' sounds like British slang for 'really do', but it just keeps half of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Estrangement is a falling out between people once close, a state of disaffection.

clue.text: Person who impresses could be even half more serious

indicators.note: half of the preceding word is kept, here its back two letters

blocks.note: the second half of even
graver is the comparative of grave, serious

explanation.surface: Someone impressive might be even a little more solemn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Person who impresses' looks like praise, but it means someone who presses marks into metal.
explanation.definitionFit: An engraver cuts designs into a surface, literally impressing marks into it.

clue.text: Squeezes water out of armbands over river

indicators.note: the armbands are over the river, covering it as an outer layer

blocks.note: inflatable swimming armbands are called water wings
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A child's swimming armbands drip water over a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'water' looks as if it belongs with the armbands (water wings), but it is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To wring cloth is to twist it hard to force the water out, as with washing.

clue.text: Heard cat rise to get bird

indicators.note: heard means we take the sound of the words, not their spelling

blocks.note: kitty is a pet name for a cat
to wake is to rise from sleep

explanation.surface: Somebody hears the cat get up and go after a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The kittiwake is a small gull of the North Atlantic coasts, so it is one kind of bird.

clue.text: Get drunk at home thanks to one getting back into brewing beer

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the letters read in the opposite direction
brewing stirs ingredients together, so these letters are mixed up
into puts one piece inside the other

blocks.note: in means at home
ta is British informal for thanks
I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone drinks at home, grateful to the person who returned to brew beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thanks to one' reads as gratitude, but it is two pieces joined and then turned round together.
explanation.definitionFit: Inebriate as a verb means to make intoxicated, the same as to get someone drunk.

clue.text: Runs away to acquire modern adventures

indicators.note: to acquire something is to take it in, so one piece gets put inside

blocks.note: escapes means runs away
AD, anno domini, marks the modern era of dates

explanation.surface: People flee to seek new and exciting experiences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'modern' as AD is a crossword convention: anno domini marks the present era of dates.
explanation.definitionFit: Escapades are daring or mischievous exploits, which are adventures of a kind.

clue.text: Typical Derwentwater view includes this tree

indicators.note: the words before it include the answer within their run of letters

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A classic view of Derwentwater, a lake in the English Lake District, features a particular tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The alder is a tree of the birch family that thrives along lakes and rivers.

clue.text: Gloomy about point average for conduct

indicators.note: about means around, so the gloomy word wraps round the rest

blocks.note: dour means gloomy
E, east, is a compass point
the mean is an average

explanation.surface: A sour remark about someone's mediocre behaviour score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' is a compass point, a common crossword source of single letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Demeanour is the way a person behaves and carries themself, which is their conduct.

clue.text: Wise comedian sent up a German after some hesitation

indicators.note: sent up in a down sense, the letters travel the opposite way
after places the reversed German word second, behind the hesitation that follows it in the clue

blocks.note: er is a hesitant sound
ein is German for a

explanation.surface: A wise comic mocks a German after pausing a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wise' looks like an adjective, but it is the surname of Ernie Wise, of the British comedy double act Morecambe and Wise.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernie Wise was the straight man of Morecambe and Wise, so the full name points to his first name.

clue.text: Sailor Chay, mast broken, heads north

indicators.note: a broken mast is in pieces, so these letters are reassembled differently

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: The sailor Chay Blyth, his mast snapped, steers northward.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Chay Blyth is a British yachtsman who sailed round the world westward, so the name fits the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A yachtsman sails yachts, so he is one particular kind of sailor.

clue.text: Set off with English doctor on old ship

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree
Noah's ark is the ancient vessel

explanation.surface: Someone departs with an English medic on board an old vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To embark is to begin a journey or venture, which is setting off.

clue.text: Music maker at bar has endless work

indicators.note: endless means without an end, so the word's final letter is dropped

blocks.note: to bar is to ban
a job is work

explanation.surface: A musician at the pub bar has an endless amount of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like the pub counter or a bar of music, but it is the verb meaning prohibit.
explanation.definitionFit: A banjo is a stringed instrument, so it is something that makes music.

clue.text: Look on as building etc is covered by flood

indicators.note: building puts things together in a construction, so these letters are arranged afresh
something covered by another is wrapped inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
a river in spate is in flood

explanation.surface: People watch as buildings and the like are swamped by a flood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' looks like a noun for a house, but it is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To spectate is to watch an event without taking part, which is to look on.

clue.text: Slice top off cakes to put ice cream in

definitions.note: a phrase describing what the answer is for, standing in for the plural noun

indicators.note: slicing off the top of a down word removes its first letter

blocks.note: scones are small cakes

explanation.surface: Instructions for trimming cakes so you can fill them with ice cream.
explanation.walkthrough: A scone is a small British baked cake, often eaten with jam and cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice cream cones are the edible wafer holders that ice cream is served in.

clue.text: I abandon family with heartless ease to get joint

indicators.note: abandoning something means leaving it behind, so that letter is removed
without a heart means the middle letters are taken out

blocks.note: taken as written
kin are your family
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone callously walks out on their family to get a joint to smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: I leaves KIN to give KN; EASE without its middle AS gives EE.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee is the hinge between thigh and lower leg, one of the body's joints.

clue.text: Upper-class comedienne ran production with private means

indicators.note: a production is something staged or made, so these letters are worked into a new form

blocks.note: U is the label for upper-class usage
taken as written

explanation.surface: A posh female comic ran a show funded from her own private wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: Unearned income comes from investments or inheritance rather than work, which is what private means are.

clue.text: Pessimistic about exercise in spaceship

indicators.note: in puts the exercise inside the following word

blocks.note: read as space (a hole, an empty space) plus ship (SS, steamship)
PE is physical education

explanation.surface: An astronaut feels gloomy about working out on board a spaceship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spaceship' looks like one word, but splits into two: space and ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hopeless has given up hope, which is to be pessimistic.

clue.text: Pickled parts of fish

indicators.note: pickled food is preserved and altered, so these letters are changed in order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Pieces of fish preserved in vinegar.
explanation.definitionFit: The sprat is a small silvery sea fish of the herring family.
